page: Microsoft Azure HB120-64rs_v3 is a virtual machine within the High Performance Computing family, provisioned through Microsoft Hyper-V. Based on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 64 dedicated physical or virtual compute cores paired with 456.0 GB of RAM. This provides approximately 7.12 GB of system memory per core, exceeding the standard ratios found in general-purpose configurations. The instance also integrates 2435 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage capabilities, while excluding hardware GPU acceleration.

The instance is built for tightly coupled engineering tasks, featuring Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) network capability. This specialized interconnect layer allows low-latency, high-throughput inter-node communication required for MPI-based clusters. With a generous allocation of 456.0 GB of memory and fast local NVMe disk arrays, the configuration avoids common I/O bottlenecks and memory saturation during memory-intensive processing cycles.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the provision of 64 dedicated cores alongside substantial memory per core makes it cost-efficient for workloads constrained by memory capacity and bandwidth rather than raw core density. By utilizing 64 cores instead of the full 120-core physical pool of the underlying platform, workloads gain more memory bandwidth per active compute thread. Tradeoffs include the total absence of discrete GPU hardware accelerators and lack of bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Microsoft Azure HB120-64rs_v3 is aligned with large-scale high-performance computing, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), numerical simulation models, and memory-heavy scientific batch processing.
